//! Fixture generator — runs at the 0.7.2 tree state ONLY.
//!
//! Writes an authentic period SQLite ledger so that later releases can prove
//! they still verify it. The point is that every byte here is produced by
//! v0.6.4's own serialisation, hashing and signing code: a fixture regenerated
//! by the release under test would prove nothing.
//!
//! At this revision `append_event_sqlite` hashes with `compute_content_hash_v2`
//! — the canonical scheme that binds `session_id` and the microsecond-truncated
//! `created_at` behind the `ELv2\0` domain tag. Paired with the v0.6.4 fixture,
//! which uses the legacy v1 layout, the two cover both halves of the
//! multi-scheme verifier.
//!
//!   ECTO_FIXTURE_OUT=/path/to/ledger.sqlite \
//!     cargo test -p ectoledger --test gen_fixture -- --nocapture

use ectoledger::ledger::sqlite::{SqliteLedger, append_event_sqlite, create_session_sqlite};
use ectoledger::schema::EventPayload;

#[tokio::test]
async fn generate_v072_fixture() {
    let out = std::env::var("ECTO_FIXTURE_OUT").expect("set ECTO_FIXTURE_OUT");
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&out);

    let ledger = SqliteLedger::connect(&format!("sqlite:{out}?mode=rwc"))
        .await
        .expect("open sqlite");
    let pool = &ledger.0;

    let (session, key) = create_session_sqlite(
        pool,
        "Audit server_config.txt for misconfigurations",
        "ollama",
        "mistral",
        Some("9f8e7d6c5b4a39281716151413121110ffeeddccbbaa99887766554433221100"),
        None,
    )
    .await
    .expect("create session");

    let sid = Some(session.id);
    let k = Some(&key);

    // A realistic short run. The exact contents matter less than the shapes:
    // the fixture exists to pin serialisation and hashing, not behaviour.
    let events = vec![
        EventPayload::Genesis {
            message: "ledger initialised".to_string(),
            nonce: Some("a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8".to_string()),
            session_public_key: Some(ectoledger::signing::public_key_hex(
                &key.verifying_key(),
            )),
        },
        EventPayload::PromptInput {
            content: "Audit server_config.txt for misconfigurations".to_string(),
        },
        EventPayload::Thought {
            content: "Reading the config file to identify misconfigurations.".to_string(),
        },
        EventPayload::Action {
            name: "read_file".to_string(),
            params: serde_json::json!({ "path": "server_config.txt" }),
        },
        EventPayload::Observation {
            content: "PermitRootLogin yes\nPort 22".to_string(),
        },
        // The old, unstructured refusal shape. 0.8.0 introduces typed
        // guard_denial / tripwire_rejection events, so this line is the reason
        // the fixture matters: prose denials written by v0.6.4 must keep
        // verifying after the enum gained variants.
        EventPayload::Thought {
            content: "Guard denied: command outside the stated audit goal".to_string(),
        },
        EventPayload::Thought {
            content: "Sufficient evidence gathered; completing.".to_string(),
        },
    ];

    for payload in &events {
        append_event_sqlite(pool, payload, sid, k)
            .await
            .expect("append");
    }

    let (seq, tip) = ectoledger::ledger::sqlite::get_latest_sqlite(pool)
        .await
        .expect("latest")
        .expect("non-empty");

    println!("FIXTURE_PATH={out}");
    println!("FIXTURE_SESSION={}", session.id);
    println!("FIXTURE_EVENTS={}", events.len());
    println!("FIXTURE_TIP_SEQUENCE={seq}");
    println!("FIXTURE_TIP_HASH={tip}");
}
